newsitem.title: UK: IPO VIEW- Viglen set to make debut on LSE.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW- Viglen set to make debut on LSE.

text.p: Viglen Technology Plc is set to be the main attraction next week in an otherwise quiet week for new issues on the London Stock Exchange.
Share dealing in Viglen is expected to begin on August 4 following the reorganisation of electronics group Amstrad Plc. Amstrad shares were suspended on July 29.
Dealers estimated Viglen shares will start trading at around 70p each.
Amstrad, which had accumulated a cash pile in excess of 200 million stg, said it could not have delivered maximum value to shareholders had it remained in its previous form.
From the reorganisation, shareholders will receive one Viglen share, 163p nominal of loan notes and a pro rata distribution of Amstrad's 69.7 percent stake of Betacom Plc in shares.

In addition, shareholders will be given a proportion of litigation notes which will represent a share of any of the net proceeds from litigation against Seagate Technology Inc, Western Digital Corporation and Western Digital UK Ltd.
Viglen made operating profits in the year to June 30 1996 of around 10.5 million stg on turnover of 106 million stg.
Also expected to make its debut next week is Blakes Clothing Plc which has been demerged from its parent Formal Group Plc .
Shares in the Essex-based fashion retailer are due to begin trading on the Alternative Investment Market on August 6 and the company is valued at around 7.2 million stg at its issue price of 72-1/2p.

Blakes has raised about four million stg from a placing and said it hoped to open three or four new stores a year in the medium term. It currently has 13 stores from West Yorkshire in the north of England to Kent in the south.
The retailer made pre-tax profits of 1.15 million stg for the year ended January 31 1997 compared to 861,000 stg for the previous year.
